Fill in at least one of the two lists

A parameter is the part of a link after the ?, for example id=5 in site.com/page?id=5. A site rule lets you choose which parameters stay and which are removed on one specific website.\nRules also apply to subdomains, so a rule for instagram.com works on www.instagram.com too.

• Domain: just the site name, like instagram.com. If you enter a full link, the site name is extracted from it.
• Always keep: parameters that must never be removed.
• Also remove: parameters to remove only on this site.
• Separate names with commas. At least one of the two lists must be filled in.

The star means “anything”. It has three uses:

1. A star at the end of a name: any parameter that starts with that text.
Example: utm_* removes all of these: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign

2. A lone star in “Also remove”: every parameter on this site.
Example: site.com/post?a=1&b=2 becomes site.com/post

3. A lone star in “Always keep”: no parameter is removed on this site.

Handy combination: put a star in “Also remove” and write only the parameters you need in “Always keep”. Everything is removed except what you listed.
Example: keep id and remove *, so site.com/post?id=5&x=1 becomes site.com/post?id=5

Note: the star only works at the end of a name. utm_* is valid, but *_source or a*b does not work. A lone star is also not accepted on the My parameters screen.

1. “Always keep” is the strongest.
2. Then “Also remove” for the same site.
3. Finally the app’s general parameter list.
If the site is in “Exception sites”, no rule is applied to it.

Domain: instagram.com
Always keep: img_index
Also remove: *

Result: all random parameters such as igsh and srtk are removed, but the post slide number (img_index) stays.

A direct https link or a GitHub file link. One rule per line, or a ClearURLs data.min.json file.
A parameter is the part of a link after the ?, for example utm_source=twitter in site.com/page?utm_source=twitter. Every parameter in this list is removed from links on all websites.

• Type one name at a time, for example fbclid.
• Names are not case sensitive.
• A star (*) at the end means “anything that starts with this”. utm_* removes utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign and the rest.
• A lone star is not allowed here. To remove every parameter on one website, use a site rule instead.
Deleting a parameter stops the app from removing it, and updating from the internet never adds it back.\nIf you delete an exact name, it is also kept when a star name such as utm_* would match it.

• The update button fetches online lists (GhostShare, AdGuard, ClearURLs) and adds only the new names.\n• Names that often break links, such as id, q, v and p, are skipped when they come from online lists.\n• The restore button brings back the default list and clears your additions and deletions.

1. Excluded websites: nothing is changed there.
2. Site rules can keep a parameter on one website.
3. This list applies to every other link.
Important YouTube parameters (v, t, start, list, index) are always protected.

A website on this list is left completely untouched: its links are not cleaned and wrapper links are not opened. Subdomains are included, so example.com also covers www.example.com and app.example.com.
Type only the site name, like example.com. If you paste a full link, the site name is taken from it automatically.
Use it when a website stops working after cleaning, for example login pages, payment pages, or one-time download links whose parameters must stay.
This list is checked first, before site rules, parameters and redirect rules. If a link is excluded, nothing else is applied to it.
The update button adds websites from the online list. The restore button empties this list.

Some apps share wrapper links such as l.facebook.com/l.php?u=… or google.com/url?q=…. They pass through a tracker before reaching the real page. When this feature is on, the app finds the real destination, cleans it, and uses it instead.
The switch at the top turns the feature on or off. When it is off, wrapper links are never opened, only cleaned. Your rules stay saved.

Each rule is a regular expression (regex) that finds the destination inside a wrapper link.
• It must start with ^http.
• It must have a group in parentheses around the destination.
• Example: ^https?://l\.example\.com/\?u=([^&]+)
The destination is read from the first group.

• Rules that are not valid are rejected when you add them and skipped when you update.\n• All rules together get a time limit of 40 milliseconds per link, so a bad rule can never freeze the phone.\n• Nested wrapper links are opened up to 3 levels deep.
The update button fetches rules from GhostShare and ClearURLs and adds only the new ones. The restore button brings back the default rules and removes the ones you added.
